Know earlier. Act sooner.

Most serious illness in India builds quietly for years before it hurts. A blood test would find it. HUMAN tests you at home, tells you the three things worth fixing, and comes back at week 12 to check that they moved.

A working app. Not yet open to everyone.

Nothing hurts. That’s the problem.

Diabetes doesn’t hurt at first. Neither does a fatty liver, a thyroid that has started to drift, PCOS, or the cholesterol that will eventually matter most.

They build for years while you feel completely normal. By the time there is a symptom, you are not preventing anything — you are managing it.

The only thing that finds them early is a blood test. Almost nobody is taking one.

  • Diabetes
  • Fatty liver

It is already most of the country.

101 million

Indians are living with diabetes.

136 million

more are close to it — and can still turn back.

More Indians are heading towards diabetes than already have it. They can still change direction. Nothing today reaches them.

And most of them have no idea.

43 of every 100

people who have diabetes do not know they have it.

A blood test would find every one of them.

Source: ICMR–INDIAB, published in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, 2023.

So we don’t sell explanations. We built the twelve weeks after the report — the part where you find out what to do, do it, and get proof that it changed.

Women

Ferritin, for every woman.

Iron deficiency is one of the most common and most missed conditions in Indian women, and you cannot find it without ferritin. It is also the marker that moves fastest once you treat it — which makes it the ideal thing to retest at week 12.

A hormone panel, when your symptoms call for it.

PCOS and PCOD have no lab support at all without sex hormones. We ask about your cycle, skin, hair and weight when you join, and order the hormone panel — FSH, LH, prolactin, oestrogen, progesterone — for the women whose answers point to it.

We don’t run it on everyone. Testing a woman with no symptoms for PCOS is over-testing, and a doctor would refuse to sign it off.

Thyroid is already in the core panel, for everyone.

Men

Testosterone, for every man.

The single most-asked-for male marker, and it is not in any standard package — including our own core. Low testosterone is common, treatable, and easy to track over time.

The markers that matter most as you get older.

Cholesterol, liver and blood sugar are all in the core panel, and they are where risk accumulates quietly through your thirties and forties.

A full hormone workup is available where results or symptoms call for it.

A 96-marker report is 96 problems. We give you three.

Three things, not ninety-six.

We rank what is worth fixing and name the one to start with this quarter. The other ninety-three are still there if you want them. Most people don’t.

This quarter’s first job.

Your LDL cholesterol is high — that’s the one that warns of heart trouble. It’s your first job this quarter.

A plan you can actually follow.

More dal and vegetables, less fried food, a twenty-minute walk after dinner. Built around food you already eat, and the levels Indian bodies actually need.

Every suggestion comes from a list a doctor has approved. The app cannot invent advice.

What to do today, and a single tap to confirm it. Workouts, medicine reminders, and a streak that quietly keeps you going.

Compared to your own past.

Every number measured against your own last result, not a textbook range built for the whole population. Normal isn’t the goal. Better than last time is.

Someone to ask.

At week 12, we come back and check.

Your retest is booked the day you join — before the motivation fades, and before life gets in the way. It’s already paid for, so cost is never the reason you skip it.

At week 10, 11 and 12, someone from our team messages you. Not a notification. A person whose job is making sure you come back.

Then we draw your blood again, and put the new number next to the old one.

Your LDL fell 14%.

That is a different experience from two PDFs, three months apart.

Then we do it again.

Six months in, the full panel runs again. Every before-and-after builds a record of what actually worked for your body — something no report can give you, because it only exists if you were there for it.

Three things we don’t sell you.

No device.

No ring, no band, no sensor. If you already wear something, we read from it. Their tracking is better than ours and will stay better — there is no reason for us to compete with it.

No supplements.

Nothing in your plan is something we profit from selling you. A company that sells you the pill has a reason to find you a deficiency. We don’t.

No explanations.

Reading a blood report used to be worth money. Any chatbot does it free now, so we give it away. What’s left worth paying for is knowing what to do, and finding out whether it worked.

What we’re looking for.

These are the conditions that build quietly, that a blood test finds, and that most people don’t know to ask for.

Show the panel for

Women

  • PCOS and PCOD

    Among the most common hormonal conditions in Indian women, and among the most missed — because the symptoms arrive one at a time and each one has an easier explanation. Irregular cycles, weight that won’t move, skin and hair changes. We ask about all of it when you join, and run the hormone panel where your answers point to it.

  • Thyroid

    It drifts slowly, and the early signs — tiredness, weight, cold, low mood — are the ones everyone dismisses. It is in the core panel for every member, every time.

  • Iron deficiency

    Extremely common, easily treated, and almost never tested for properly. Iron studies alone won’t find it — you need ferritin, and ferritin costs a third of the price of the entire 96-marker panel on its own, which is why it isn’t in a standard package. It is in ours, for every woman.

  • Blood sugar, cholesterol and liver

    The three that build for years with no symptoms at all. Everyone gets these.

Men

  • Testosterone

    Common to run low, straightforward to treat, and absent from almost every standard package. Fatigue, weight, mood and motivation all sit downstream of it. It is included for every man.

  • Blood sugar and insulin resistance

    The window where things can still turn back is years long and completely silent. This is the group the 136 million belong to.

  • Cholesterol and heart risk

    The number that matters most is rarely the one people know to ask about. We show you which of yours is doing the damage.

  • Liver

    Fatty liver is now extremely common in Indian men who would describe themselves as healthy, and it is reversible when you catch it early.

Built here, for bodies here.

Indian reference levels.

Indian bodies carry risk at different thresholds. A cholesterol number that is fine in a European reference range is not automatically fine here, and neither is a waist measurement. We use the levels that apply to you.

Indian food.

Your plan is built out of what is already in your kitchen. More dal, different oil, the walk after dinner. Not almond flour and quinoa.

Blood drawn at your door.

Labs already collect at home across 2,500+ towns. We use that network rather than building our own, which is the only reason a yearly membership works at this price.

Your cycle, if you have one.

Results read differently at different points in a cycle. The app syncs it, and takes it into account rather than ignoring it.

Who stands behind the advice.

A doctor decides what the app is allowed to say.

Every suggestion in your plan comes from a protocol a doctor has approved. The coach can answer anything you ask, but it can only answer from that protocol. It cannot invent advice, and it cannot go beyond what has been signed off.

Someone whose job is getting you back.

A care coordinator handles your bookings, your scheduling, and the week 10, 11 and 12 messages. Not automated reminders — a person.

And a scope we’re clear about.

HUMAN informs and supports your care. It is not a diagnosis, it does not replace your doctor, and if a result looks urgent we will tell you to see one.

A note from the founder

I’m Aadit. I’m studying nutrition and dietetics, and I built the first version of HUMAN on my own because I couldn’t find anything that did the part I actually wanted — the twelve weeks after the report.

I built a company before this one and it failed. I learned more from that than from anything that worked. It’s also why the first person I brought in here is a doctor, not a marketer.

We’re opening to a small first group.

The founding cohort is limited, and everyone in it pays the same price with no discounts. We’d rather start with a few people and get it right than open to everyone and find out later.

About this file

This is the HUMAN home page as a single HTML file, with the stylesheet, both typefaces and all eight app screens embedded. Nothing loads from the network, so it opens the same way on a plane as on a desk.

What is here: every one of the fifteen sections, at full fidelity — layout, type, colour, the marker rows, the four charts, the phone frames. The Body toggle works, the waitlist modal opens, the mobile menu opens. Resize the window and the layout responds exactly as the real site does.

What is not: the motion. Every reveal, the four pinned scenes and the sticky phone rail need the running site — what you see here is the state each animation ends in, which is also what the site shows a visitor with JavaScript disabled. The other pages and the working waitlist form need the app too: cd site && npm install && npm run dev.

The app screens are placeholders at the exact export dimensions, 1170 × 2532. Real screenshots drop over them without changing any layout.
